A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TIP-I2V. All 17 pages of each version, including supplementary Sections 7–17, are readable and support matching the text, tables, figures, and technical details.

before.justification: v1 reports original user-preference analyses, image-to-video benchmarking, and trained detection and source-image retrieval experiments, including Figures 4–6 and Tables 3–5 and 7.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical analyses and experimental results in the main text and supplement.

M1.justification: The generation pipeline, VideoMAE detector, and CosFace/ViT retrieval baseline remain unchanged. Anonymous UserIDs are newly documented metadata; the PDFs do not establish a changed modeling procedure. GPT-4o direction extraction was already described in v1 Section 10.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same TIP-I2V corpus and retain the same prompt-analysis, video-generation evaluation, video-origin classification, and source-image retrieval coverage through TIP-Eval, TIP-ID, and TIP-Trace. No evaluated population, domain, or task scenario is added.

E2.justification: The five evaluated generation models, seven fake-image detectors plus Blind Guess in Table 3, and 19 pretrained retrieval comparators in Table 5 are unchanged. Removing Movie Gen from a future-extension example does not remove an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: TIP-Eval retains 1,000 subjects, 10,000 prompts, and ten evaluation dimensions. The TIP-ID 9:1 split, TIP-Trace set sizes, same/cross-domain protocols, preprocessing, and training budgets in supplementary Sections 9 and 13–16 are unchanged.

E4.justification: The semantic-distribution comparisons, user-preference analyses, subject-specific quality examples, misinformation case, and cross-domain generalization analyses are retained. The supplementary examples and analyses add no new ablation or robustness evidence.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed lists, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The point-estimate reporting practice is unchanged.

E6.justification: The numerical tables, plotted results, and empirical findings match. For example, Table 4 retains average same/cross-domain accuracies of 96.3%/87.2%, and Table 5 retains retrieval scores of 89.1%/84.7% µAP. Supplementary Table 7 is also unchanged.

T1.justification: Neither version introduces theoretical propositions or proofs. The retained metric explanations, dataset-size calculations, and mathematical reasoning in the supplementary material are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims: a first large-scale image-to-video prompt dataset, its distinction from existing prompt datasets, and applications to user preferences, evaluation, and misinformation research.

C2.justification: Section 5.5 replaces the retrieval-augmented generation suggestion with pre-generating and caching videos to accelerate future generation, conditional on sufficiently mature models. The introduction clarifies preference-guided video collection, and Section 17 refines the explanation of anonymization. Existing experimental interpretations and generalization limitations remain.

D1.justification: Section 3 and Figure 2 newly document anonymous UserIDs derived from user names. Conversely, Section 14 replaces the precise MCG-NJU/videomae-base checkpoint location with a generic official-repository description, and several tool URLs disappear from the references. Other implementation settings and the project address remain.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, substantive novelty positioning, and bibliography membership are retained. Movie Gen disappears from a prospective extension example but remains in the bibliography; added citation markers refer to already-cited works.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized wording edits to the abstract, introductory prompt examples, metadata description, future-research discussion, and social-impact paragraph. Bibliographic formatting is simplified. The overall narrative and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is rearranged to display UserID and Direction fields, with an updated caption. Other caption, sizing, spacing, and text-flow adjustments occur, including reference-page reflow. The experimental tables, plots, and supplementary image examples retain their content.

improvement.justification: v2 improves metadata transparency by documenting anonymous UserIDs and clarifying their privacy role. However, removing the exact VideoMAE checkpoint identifier and several tool links makes reproduction less precise. With unchanged empirical support, these opposing documentation changes do not establish a reliable net improvement or deterioration.
